body:
closes #47695

When every valid value in a column/row/table is equal, matplotlib's `Normalize` fills its whole output with 0, NaN included. `Styler.background_gradient` and `Styler.text_gradient` then gave those NaN cells the lowest colormap color instead of the missing-value color the colormap gives NaN everywhere else. This keeps NaN as NaN after normalizing so it always maps to the colormap's missing-value color (including a custom one set via `with_extremes(bad=...)`).

AI disclosure: drafted with Claude Code (`claude opus 5.5 (high)`), which diagnosed the bug, wrote the fix and test, and ran review passes comparing styled output against main.
title: BUG: Styler.background_gradient colors NaN as the lowest value when vmin == vmax (GH#47695)
